summary: A short note from Alex McKenzie at BBN that attaches network traffic statistics for the ARPANET for September 1972. The tables show how many packets each host sent over the period. BBN had been giving these figures to ARPA each month and now shared them with the whole network community.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC contains a table of ARPANET packet output for September 1972. The table separates traffic between nodes from traffic within nodes and lists totals for each host.

questions: how much traffic did each arpanet host send
how many packets were sent in september 1972
subtitle: Host packet-output totals for the ARPANET in September 1972.

tldr.problem: RFC 400 publishes network traffic statistics for September 1972 as a table of host throughput.
tldr.mechanism: The attached summary counts packet output by host, separating inter-node and intra-node traffic and providing daily figures.
tldr.outcome: The report gives totals for the month but does not explain a broader measurement method in its short accompanying note.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 400 as Unknown and says it updates RFC 391. It is a historical ARPANET traffic table for September 1972.

sections.title: September Traffic Tables
sections.content:
Alex McKenzie attaches network traffic statistics for September 1972. The main table is headed Host Throughput Summary (Packet Output) and lists host throughput by site and host number.

The table includes inter-node, intra-node and total packet counts, along with average daily internode traffic and the number of days counted.
sections.plainLanguage: The attached report counts packets sent by hosts during September. It shows traffic to other nodes separately from traffic within a node.

sections.title: Host and Site Entries
sections.content:
The summary includes entries for sites such as UCLA, SRI, UCSB, BBN, MIT, RAND, Harvard, Lincoln, Stanford and others. Some sites have several host rows followed by a subtotal. TINK, MC CL and BELV are marked as having no traffic.

The report includes a total of 24,867,510 inter-node packets and 7,589,632 intra-node packets, and gives daily averages and an average per node-day.
sections.plainLanguage: Each site is listed with one or more host entries, and some sites have subtotals. The report also gives totals across the listed traffic.

sections.title: Scope of the Note
sections.content: The RFC's accompanying text only says that September statistics are attached. It updates RFC 391 according to the unit metadata and does not explain the table's detailed collection process.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC is mainly a statistical table, not a protocol description. Its metadata says it updates RFC 391.
